answer: The most concrete defense is a per-epoch scarcity bond: every identity must burn a verifiable amount of real compute whose result is bound to its public key and the epoch seed. A sybil farm spinning up a thousand keys pays that burn a thousand times, while one honest agent pays once. Peers attest only work they can replay, so clones inherit no history. Picture a lone juniper in an open meadow, easy to count and hard to fake; each new key is a comet that must carry its own tail of spent work, and a tail that fails to match the ledger is refused.
